epv.note: Price above EPV: the market pays for growth. EPV above tangible book: the business earns more than its assets would cost to rebuild — a sign of a moat (Greenwald). EPV below tangible book: the assets earn less than their cost.

implied_return.note: The yearly return a buyer at today's price earns if each model's assumptions hold (an implied cost of capital). Above the cost of equity: the price leaves room; below: the price already asks for more than the models deliver.

methods.formula: 10-year Monte Carlo: revenue growth switches between high / steady / decline regimes by a Markov chain; margin drifts by regime; value = Σ discounted FCFF − SBC + terminal, per share

methods.formula: Stage-weighted value = Σ weight × central value of the stage's methods (weights renormalized over the methods available)
steps: 25% × $51.91 (DCF — Monte Carlo 10th–90th percentile) + 25% × $36.17 (Outside view — base-rate Monte Carlo) + 15% × $23.23 (EV/Sales vs Rule of 40 (all-company fit)) + 15% × $48.90 (EV/Sales vs peers) + 20% × $73.80 (P/E vs peers) = $47.60
assumptions: fixed by stage before any result was seen (base_rates.STAGES)
methods.fit: Its stage is “High growth” — revenue growth +28.9% — which fixes these methods and their weights in advance.

methods.formula: Value = (assets in place + C − net debt) ÷ shares;  C = S·N(d₁) − K·e^(−rT)·N(d₂), d₁ = [ln(S ÷ K) + (r + σ²/2)T] ÷ σ√T, d₂ = d₁ − σ√T
steps: S = the expansion in year 5: the revenue it adds $22.03B (to $38.98B) × margin 29.2% × (1 − tax), as a growing perpetuity, discounted = $45.44B

σ = 47% (its stock, a year of daily closes), T = 5 years, r = 4.91% → C = $25.64B
assets in place = NOPAT $4.02B ÷ WACC = $45.12B; value = ($45.12B + $25.64B − net debt $6.69B) ÷ 1,675,360,395 = $38.24
